title: The Little Bear and the Storm
summary: A night full of thunder frightens little Nilo the bear, until Mama Bear teaches him a secret trick to calm his heart.

scenes.text:
Night was falling over the forest, and little Nilo the bear was snuggled up in his cozy cave, next to Mama Bear. Outside, the trees began to bend under a rising wind. Many drops of rain started to fall on the leaves.

Nilo yawned and closed his eyes, ready to sleep. But suddenly, far away, there rolled a rumble of thunder.

It was still very soft, like a sleeping drum. Nilo opened his eyes wide, wide. He felt a little knot in his tummy.

'Mama,' he whispered, 'what was that noise? ' Mama Bear hugged him gently and said, 'It's just the storm, my love. Nothing is going to happen to you.

'

The storm grew stronger. Over the cave whistled the wind.

And all of a sudden, BOOM!, over the roof rolled a huge clap of thunder. Nilo hid under the blanket and began to tremble.

'I'm scared, mama,' he said in a shaky little voice. 'The thunder is so loud. ' Mama Bear searched for him among the blankets and pulled him close to her warm chest.

She felt Nilo's heart beating very fast, thump-thump, thump-thump. 'I know, sweetheart,' she said tenderly. 'Sometimes big noises are scary.

But I am here with you, and together we will wait for it to pass. '

'Do you want me to teach you a secret trick? ' asked Mama Bear. Nilo peeked out his nose and said yes.

'It is easy: when the noise comes, instead of trembling, we are going to breathe.

' Just then, over the forest, rolled another rumble of thunder. Mama Bear took air in through her nose, filling her belly like a balloon: oooone, two, three. Then she let the air out slowly through her mouth: whooo.

'Now you,' she said. Nilo took air in deep, filled his tummy, and then let it out softly. Again.

And again. Little by little, the knot in his belly came undone, like a bow that unties itself.

Outside, the storm went on, but Nilo and Mama Bear breathed together, calm. After a while, over the cave, there rolled another rumble of thunder. This time Nilo took his air in slowly instead of hiding.

'I did it, mama! ' he whispered, a little bit proud. Mama Bear smiled and gave him a kiss on the forehead.

Outside, the rain began to fall more softly, in tiny drops that slid down the leaves: drip, drip, drip.

The wind was not whistling so hard anymore. The rumbles drifted farther and farther away, as if the storm were sleepy too, and were walking home to its house.

And then, without noticing, the storm passed. Mama Bear poked her head out of the cave. 'Look, Nilo,' she said softly.

The sky was clear and, one by one, out came the stars. They looked like friendly little lights. A round moon lit up the wet forest, and everything was calm.

Nilo took a deep breath one last time and smiled. He was not scared anymore. Curled up in his mama's warm arms, with heavy eyes, he let sleep wrap around him.

'Good night, my brave one,' whispered Mama Bear. And so, peaceful, until the next morning, little Nilo fell asleep.
